expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | (SubscriptionBase & { status: 'trialing'; trialEndsAt: Date }) | ... each variant with unique status literal

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each intersection type in the union carries only its own fields—trialEndsAt in trialing only, renewsAt in active only, etc.

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never) {...} with default: return assertNever(sub) in nextBillingEvent switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Brands SubscriptionId and CustomerId, but planId is left as bare string: 'planId: string' without branding

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function provided; only shows nextBillingEvent example, which is not a state-change constraint

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Names: 'A bag of optionals', 'A switch that silently ignores a fifth status', 'You cannot construct an active sub with a cancel reason, or a canceled one without voluntary'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Opens by contrasting against 'A bag of optionals (trialEndsAt?, retryCount?, ...) claims 2^7 states are legal; four are' then recommends union as solution
